target_customer: Recruiting and staffing agencies (permanent, executive search, contract, temp and RPO)
problem: Recruiters lose time to manual logging and clunky ATS tools that store data without using it, and legacy platforms cannot support AI natively.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (comparison pages list about 149 USD per user per month)
product_category: AI native ATS and CRM for recruiting firms

founders.name: Lander Degreve
founders.background_notes: YC page: built an AI job match tool at Bain, JPMorgan investment banking internship.

founders.name: Manu Vanderveeren
education: London Business School, Master's in Financial Analysis
founders.background_notes: YC page: internships at Morgan Stanley and CVC.

founders.name: Samuel Smeys
founders.background_notes: YC page: built data and ML pipelines for recruitment agencies at BCG.

competitors.name: Bullhorn
competitors.what: Incumbent ATS and CRM for staffing agencies; named by Spott's YC launch as the alternative target

competitors.name: Loxo
competitors.what: ATS with AI features for agencies; named by Spott's YC launch as the alternative target

technical_complexity.rationale: A full ATS and CRM plus AI agents, matching, outreach and migration tools is a large product surface, and the company says it built it from scratch to be AI native.

defensibility.rationale: Agencies store years of candidate data in their ATS so migration is sticky once won, and the company offers a white glove migration to lower the barrier. Many rivals market AI native ATS products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI features and several competitors (Recruiterflow, Jarvi, Globus.ai) positioned as AI native by 2026; no acquisition of Spott found.

market_need_then: The founders saw agencies losing time to manual logging while consulting for them. Customers named on the site migrated from Bullhorn, Loxo, Vincere, JobAdder and others.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, punchy and informal with wordplay (Outp(l)ace everyone) and taglines like Recruiting, without limits.

branding.community_and_virality: Founders posts and trade press covered the Series A across many outlets in 2026-09; company runs comparison pages against Bullhorn and others.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct voice and lots of funding press, but the double t spelling is easy to mistype and no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.to: Full AI native ATS and CRM
pivots.why: Mid program decision per the company origin story, after concluding legacy platform architecture could not support AI; month is approximate to the YC batch

outcome_analysis: Spott started in November 2024, pivoted during YC from a report writer to a full AI native ATS, raised a 3.2M seed and then a 21M Series A led by Balderton in September 2026. The company says ARR passed 1M euros by about February 2026 and 500 plus agencies use it. These are company claims and the later growth rests on a crowded market with several AI native rivals.
notes: Seed date conflicts: the company origin story says March 2025, while the company press page shows a Sep 21, 2026 stamp and a search snippet mentions a January 2026 announcement; March 2025 used. Series A press dates differ (2026-09-22 vs 2026-10-06 in one aggregator). Total funding 24.2M and valuation above 100M USD are founder or press claims, so no post_money recorded. Founders' consulting employers (McKinsey, BCG, Bain) are from the origin story and YC page. Competitor entries cite the YC launch positioning rather than independent dated coverage.
